page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 925.36 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 153.41 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 86.39 GB/sec. CPU performance is generally average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1893.0 and a multi-core score of 10109.0. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the top 25% at 14.47 GB/sec, whereas encryption capabilities are weaker, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%. Large language model inference speeds are mixed, showing average performance for text generation on a 7B model (11.81 tokens/sec) but poor performance for prompt processing on the same model (15.63 tokens/sec).

The r8gb.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its high memory density per core and the power-efficient ARMv9 architecture. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization overhead. This hardware profile is suited for memory-bound applications such as database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive data processing. However, workloads requiring high cryptographic throughput, local NVMe storage, or GPU acceleration are constrained by the hardware design.
